findings.title: LDs not specified as sole remedy
findings.deviation: The clause states that penalties are credited against damage claims rather than being the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.
findings.impact: AtliQ remains potentially liable for actual damages that exceed the 5% contractual penalty cap.
findings.quote: The contractual penalty shall be credited against any claim for damages for the same delay.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs where the delay is caused by the client; LDs are the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Extended confidentiality duration
findings.deviation: The confidentiality obligation lasts for five years post-termination, exceeding the standard 2–3 year preference.
findings.impact: AtliQ must maintain confidentiality protocols and records for an extended period after the engagement ends.
findings.quote: The confidentiality obligation shall continue for five (5) years after termination of this Agreement.

fine.note: Liability is capped at 1x total remuneration with standard statutory carve-outs for German law.
The mutual indemnity for breach and IP infringement aligns with the playbook.
Ownership of deliverables vests upon payment and AtliQ retains rights to PipeKit as background IP.
The 10-day review period and deemed acceptance mechanism meet AtliQ's standards.
Termination for convenience provides for payment of services rendered and committed costs.
The DPA and SCC framework for EU-India data transfer is standard for this jurisdiction.
The agreement contains no non-compete or non-solicit restrictions.
The contract does not impose specific insurance requirements or limits.
The 12-month warranty period for software deliverables is standard.
The payment clause excludes deductions, effectively preventing unauthorized set-off.
